```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(L0glm)
options(width=95, digits=3)
```

L0glm fits sparse generalized linear models using adaptive ridge and IRLS.
The same interface covers ordinary GLMs, negative binomial counts, joint
multinomial classification and Cox survival models. Dense and sparse designs,
multiple responses and very large predictor sets share one fitting interface.

## Install

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tomwenseleers/L0glm", subdir="L0glm")
library(L0glm)
```

Windows source installation requires [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).

## Start with a small model

Pass a design matrix and a response vector to `l0glmFit()`. A GIC preset
provides a single penalty value for variable selection. A relaxed refit
then estimates the retained effects with reduced shrinkage.

```{r small-fit}
sim <- simul("normal", n=200L, p=80L, n_nonzero=6L, seed=42L)
small <- l0glmFit(sim$X, sim$y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic")
which(as.numeric(coef(small)) != 0)
head(fitted(small))
```

The coefficient vector retains the original predictor positions, with zeroes
at excluded predictors. For a response matrix, `grouped=TRUE` selects predictor
rows shared by the responses. See [fitting controls](controls.html) for
weights, offsets and constraints.

## Fit a sparse model

Here 60 positive or negative effects are hidden among **one million predictors**
with 1,000 observations. A single call fits the model using the package defaults.
The dense design occupies about 8 GB; data generation is excluded from the fitting time.

```{r million, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
n <- 1000L
p <- 1000000L
X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p)
active <- sample.int(p, 60L)
beta <- numeric(p)
beta[active] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8)
set.seed(1)
y <- as.numeric(X[, active] %*% beta[active]) + rnorm(n)

system.time(fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=gaussian()))
l0glmMetrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[
  c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
```

<!-- BEGIN million-metrics -->
| Seconds | GIC | TP | FP | FN | TN | F1 | MCC |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2.63 | 4194 | 46 | 0 | 14 | 999940 | 0.868 | 0.876 |
<!-- END million-metrics -->

<img src="../million-coefficients.png" alt="True versus estimated coefficients for the one-million-predictor default L0glm fit." width="100%">

The true coefficients are used to evaluate recovery. Fitting uses only `X` and
`y`. Returned coefficients retain all one million rows in a sparse matrix.
The default automatic screening uses the available physical cores; set
`screen.nthreads=1L` for serial screening.

## Tune a regularization path

The preset already gives a strong sparse model. This tuning path uses the
predictor pool found by ISIS at the preset. Each lambda fits its own model
within that pool, so the graph shows how the penalty changes selection
on a common set of candidates. The grid includes the GIC preset.

<!-- BEGIN million-path-summary -->
The best grid value is **26.70**, with a GIC preset of **26.70**.
<!-- END million-path-summary -->

```{r path, eval=FALSE}
tuned <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), tune="gic",
  nlambda=10L, prop_range=.25, screen.path="preset", coefs.true=beta, plot=TRUE)
c(lambda_best=tuned$lambda_best, lambda_preset=tuned$lambda_preset)
```

<img src="../million-path.png" alt="Coefficient paths and GIC for a shared ISIS candidate pool in the million-predictor example." width="100%">

The graph uses a reversed `log10(lambda)` axis, with strong regularization on
the left and support sizes above the panels. `prop_range=.25` focuses on the
preset; use `prop_range=1` to explore the full numerical path.
Use `screen.path="independent"` to rerun ISIS at each penalty and allow
the candidate set to change.
For five-fold cross-validation use `tune="cv", nfolds=5L`. See
[model selection and cross-validation](selection.html) for a larger signal-rich
example, confidence bars and the one-standard-error model.

## Predict and inspect

```{r predict, eval=FALSE}
predict(fit, X[1:5, , drop=FALSE])
summary(fit)
c(logLik=as.numeric(logLik(fit)), AIC=AIC(fit), BIC=BIC(fit), GIC=GIC(fit))
predict(tuned$fit_best, X[1:5, , drop=FALSE])
```

`fitted(fit)` returns fitted means for the training observations; `predict()`
applies the model in the original predictor coordinates.

## Choose a workflow

| Task | Main function |
|---|---|
| One fast preset fit | `l0glmFit(X, y, family=...)` |
| Tune an information criterion | `l0glmTune(..., tune="gic")` |
| Cross-validate prediction deviance | `l0glmTune(..., tune="cv", nfolds=5)` |
| Compare sparse regression methods | `sparseGLM()` |
| Score predictions and support recovery | `l0glmMetrics()` |
| Control high dimensional prescreening | `screen="auto"`, `"SIS"` or `"ISIS"` |

The default `screen="auto"` enables ISIS exactly when `p_eligible > 10*n`.
Here `n` is the number of training rows, and `p_eligible` excludes mandatory
terms and predictors excluded by zero starts in every response channel.
`l0glmTune()` applies this rule independently within each full-data or CV
training fit, without a separate minimum sample size or predictor count.

Continue with [SIS / ISIS screening](high-dimensional.html),
[single and multichannel deconvolution](deconvolution.html),
[weights and validation](controls.html), or the
[negative binomial](negative-binomial.html), [multinomial](multinomial.html)
and [Cox](cox.html) examples.
